postings.title: Senior Software Engineer, Platform
postings.description:
About Us
Creditspring is a new way of borrowing that puts its members first. We are an FCA-regulated fintech and one of the UK's only subscription finance companies: members pay a fixed monthly fee and borrow with no interest. Since 2016 we have made 1.7 million loans to more than 450,000 active members. Our mission is to make credit fairer, clearer and safer.
We won Best Consumer Credit Product at the Credit Awards 2024 and Responsible Lender of the Year 2024. We are in The Sunday Times 100 Tech (2025 and 2026) and the Sifted 100 UK & Ireland. We are about 150 people.
We chose Ruby on Rails from the start and we still love it: it lets a small team move fast in a regulated industry. We stay at most one major version behind across all our systems, and we clean up tech debt as we go. Currently our apps run on Rails 8 and are deployed to AWS and Heroku.
We record every change as a business event, such as a loan approved or a repayment received, and share those events over Kafka. Events are our source of truth: when we needed to, we have rebuilt our database tables from them.
We work with non-technical colleagues to understand the why behind the what. We write descriptive tests with RSpec and take ownership of our features end to end. Every change gets a review. We keep pull requests small and ship many times a day.
We have built a remote culture around short, clear writing on Basecamp that people actually want to read, few meetings, and team gatherings at our London office.
We are open to two ways of working for this role:

- 
A fully remote contractor who can be based anywhere +/-5 hours of GMT.
- 
As an employee who will be based in our London office and work in a hybrid pattern of 2 days per week in our office. If you are based in the UK you must be applying as an employee.
About the role
We are hiring to finish one shift and to keep building the foundations for more products. More and more, our member app and our operations app ask Platform for a decision or a payment, then react to the events that follow. This abstraction frees those product teams to focus on our members, and lets us add foundation features without touching their code.
Platform owns the four services that every loan depends on:

- 
Underwriting makes every credit decision we take. It pulls data from the credit agencies and open banking and decides who we can lend to.
- 
Payments moves every pound: loans out to members, and repayments and membership fees back in. Faster Payments, Direct Debits, Debit Cards, Open Banking payments. We are always looking for more ways to make it easy to move money for our members.
- 
Webhooks receives everything our partners send us, from payment updates to identity checks. We never want to lose a message.
- 
Data Mill is our relational data warehouse. It powers the live monitoring we rely on every day, while we move its heavier reporting work to our new data lakehouse.
These services sit at the edge of our system. They talk to the outside world, from credit agencies to payment providers, and turn what comes back into our own events. If one of these stops, the business stops.
The Underwriting team sets our lending rules. We make them easy to apply at scale. Our customers are the other engineering teams, and our job is to give them a reliable, well-documented foundation to build on.
We started the Platform work in 2025 to pull core lending capabilities out of our two main Rails apps and into services that each do one thing well. It already pays off for our members:

- 
Moving underwriting into its own service made our credit decisions faster, so applicants get a yes or no for their loan sooner.
- 
Payments always have a backup provider we can switch to, so money keeps moving even when a payment provider goes down.
We extract only when the need is worth the cost, and Platform owns that agenda: when to extract, what, and how.
You will join a team of three engineers, and report to the Platform engineering manager.
Responsibilities

- 
Design, build and run the Ruby/Rails services every product depends on: Underwriting, Payments, Webhooks and Mill.
- 
Decide with the team when core lending logic should move out of our main apps and into a service, and do it without breaking a business that works.
- 
Integrate with credit agencies, open banking and payment providers, and make those integrations dependable.
- 
Keep our services healthy: Ruby and Rails upgrades, security fixes and regular audits of what we own.
- 
Take on hard reliability problems. For example: how do we make sure we never lose a message from a partner, and recover cleanly when processing fails? You find the answer with the team.
- 
Raise the bar on reliability across the company, not only in our own services: incident playbooks, disaster recovery tests, and alerts that fire before our members notice a problem.
- 
Make production easy to understand for every engineer: logs, metrics and errors with enough context to find the cause fast.
- 
Improve the developer experience for all our engineering teams: one catalogue of our services, clear documentation, fast and reliable CI, and tools that make debugging easier. We are already trying an AI agent that reads our logs and errors to help find the cause of a problem.
- 
Work with our Engineering, Data, Underwriting and Risk teams, who are your customers.
- 
Share what you know. Write it down and review code, so anyone on the team can pick up any service. 
What you'll need to succeed

- 
Experience finding the boundaries in a monolith and moving one part out behind a clear contract, or running a set of services that talk over APIs and events (we use Kafka).
- 
You design for failure: idempotency, retries and background jobs (Sidekiq).
- 
Solid PostgreSQL knowledge, including query performance.
- 
Experience with third-party integrations, ideally payments, credit data or banking APIs.
- 
You have set up observability for production systems: what to measure, what to alert on, and how to make an error easy to trace.
- 
You enjoy building tools that make other engineers faster.
- 
Comfortable running services on AWS. You will work closely with our Cloud engineer.
- 
Nice to have: fintech or lending experience, event sourcing, domain-driven design, developer portals (such as Backstage), CI tuning.
About you

- 
Coding and deploying is just the beginning of owning a feature.
- 
You want to solve real problems for our members and our business.
- 
You trust automated testing to keep what you build reliable and easy to maintain.
- 
You know the Ruby ecosystem well. You know which gems to trust, and when to write your own.
- 
You are pragmatic and always improving. You don't pick a shiny tool for its own sake.
Why work with us

- 
Members who love us. We help people go from debt to savings without stress. Very few finance companies get reviews like these.
- 
Small projects, small teams. We use our own version of Shape Up by 37signals. Projects are small (six weeks at the median), teams are small and focused, and each team picks its own day-to-day way of working.
- 
We learn from each other. We demo our work often. We debate the design, then pick the pragmatic option together. The write-ups are so good that other teams reuse them.
- 
Pragmatic about AI. We use AI where it helps, and not where it hurts how we work. On critical systems, people read the code and stay in the loop. Where the stakes are low, we experiment freely. We decide together, case by case, based on fit and our appetite for risk.

Don’t meet all the listed requirements? Research shows that women and people of underrepresented groups often don't apply for jobs unless they're 100% qualified. As an equal opportunities employer, we know that diversity is a key part of our teams' successes - so if your experience doesn’t fit perfectly but this role excites you, we’d love for you to apply. We’re committed to Creditspring being an inclusive environment where employees feel welcomed, valued and listened to; we want you to thrive as your true self.

Please note that the People Team is contactable only via people@creditspring.co. Unsolicited emails to other team members will not be actioned.

postings.title: Head of Product
postings.description:
We are Creditspring, a new way of borrowing that focuses on its members and provides them with safe and efficient short-term financial products.
As one of the UK’s only subscription finance company in the market, Creditspring is a profitable, FCA-regulated fintech on a mission to make credit fairer, clearer and safer. Members pay a small, fixed monthly fee to access no-interest loans, knowing the total cost upfront, with no hidden charges or confusing APRs. We’ve provided over 1.7 million loans to 450,000+ active members.
Our approach has won Best Consumer Credit Product (Credit Awards 2024) and Responsible Lender of the Year 2024, with places in The Sunday Times 100 Tech 2025 and the Sifted 100 UK & Ireland. Now we’re growing from our lending membership into a multi-product business.
We are offering up to £155k + company bonus for this opportunity.
About the role
Creditspring is a profitable UK fintech built around a simple idea: borrowing should be easier to understand and manage. We’re building on our award-winning lending membership to become a multi-product business, developing new propositions and growing existing products like Creditspring Go, which helps members work towards eligibility for a loan.
As Head of Product, you’ll lead and grow our Product team across the UK and India. You’ll directly manage the two Product Leads, who lead the Product Managers across two areas:

- 
Membership and loan origination. How customers join, apply, borrow and renew, including how we develop our membership and launch new propositions.
- 
Loan servicing and customer operations. How members manage and repay their loans, how we support customers in financial difficulty, and the platforms and tools that make this possible.
Responsibilities

- 
Manage and develop the Product Leads. Coach them as managers, set clear expectations for their teams, and give honest, timely feedback. Work with each Lead to grow future leaders within their teams.
- 
Shape and grow the Product team. Decide how responsibilities should sit across the teams as the portfolio grows. Work with the CPO on bigger changes to team structure and headcount, plan the skills and roles we’ll need as the business expands, and lead Product hiring across the UK and India.
- 
Own both roadmaps. Decide what to prioritise, sequence, pause or stop based on customer need, commercial value, risk and capacity. Lead planning and performance reviews, and adapt how they work as we grow.
- 
Be a trusted partner to the CPO. Keep the CPO informed about performance, decisions and emerging risks. Raise issues early and bring a clear recommendation when a decision needs executive input. Challenge assumptions constructively and represent Product in executive discussions when needed.
- 
Work closely with Engineering and Design. Shape solutions together early, make trade-offs on scope and sequencing, and balance new launches and improvements to existing journeys with investment in the platforms they depend on.
- 
Own product performance and improve how we use data. Build a close partnership with the Data & Analytics team. Help Product Leads and PMs improve what they track and how they track it, from agreeing on metrics and baselines to making sure the right data is captured before launch. Connect signals across customer behaviour, research, operational performance and unit economics. Bring the CPO a clear view of what’s changing across the portfolio, what’s likely driving it and what you recommend doing next.
- 
Extend how Product uses AI. Build on the team’s existing use of AI in day-to-day work, including dashboard building. Coach Product Leads and PMs to find and test new uses in discovery, analysis and prototyping. Help the team share practices that improve the speed or quality of its work, and set clear expectations for checking outputs and handling data responsibly.
- 
Build and grow responsibly. Bring in Marketing and Finance as you develop business cases and launch new propositions. Involve Credit Risk, Underwriting, Operational Risk, Compliance and Customer Operations early so that Consumer Duty shapes how products are designed, launched and monitored, including how we assess fair value and support customers in vulnerable circumstances.
What you'll need to succeed

- 
Experience managing product leaders who themselves manage others. You can show how you’ve coached managers, handled performance issues and developed people for bigger roles.
- 
Experience shaping how Product teams are organised and growing them through hiring and internal development, including across locations or time zones.
- 
A track record of owning roadmaps and product outcomes across multiple teams in a regulated consumer business. Experience in UK consumer lending, particularly in origination or servicing, is especially valuable.
- 
The judgement to know which decisions to make, when to involve executives and how to give them a clear recommendation. You’re comfortable raising difficult issues and challenging senior stakeholders constructively.
- 
Evidence of working successfully with Engineering and Design on complex products, from discovery and technical trade-offs through launch and ongoing improvement.
- 
Strong analytical and commercial judgement. You’ve worked with an analytics team to improve what Product tracks and how it tracks it. You can connect customer behaviour, operational data and unit economics to explain what’s driving performance and recommend what to do next.
- 
The ability to change course. You can show when new evidence or a shift in business priorities led you to revisit a decision, explain what changed and why, and align teams and stakeholders around the revised plan.
- 
Hands-on experience using AI in product work. You can show where AI improved the speed or quality of your own work, how you helped others use it effectively, and where you exercised judgement about data and the reliability of outputs.
Why join us?

- 
Help shape what Creditspring becomes next. Join a profitable business as it grows into a multi-product company. You’ll help decide where to invest, how to grow established products like Go, and how new propositions fit together for members.
- 
Make a difference at moments that matter. Your decisions will shape how people understand their borrowing options, manage their repayments and get support when money is tight.
- 
Build the team for the next stage of growth. You’ll have the scope to develop two Product Leads, shape how teams work across the UK and India, and invest in the skills they’ll need as the portfolio grows.

Don’t meet all the listed requirements? Research shows that women and people of underrepresented groups often don't apply for jobs unless they're 100% qualified. As an equal opportunities employer, we know that diversity is a key part of our teams' successes - so if your experience doesn’t fit perfectly but this role excites you, we’d love for you to apply. We’re committed to Creditspring being an inclusive environment where employees feel welcomed, valued and listened to; we want you to thrive as your true self.

Please note that the People Team is contactable only via people@creditspring.co. Unsolicited emails to other team members will not be actioned.

postings.title: IT Support
postings.description:
We are Creditspring, a new way of borrowing that focuses on its members and provides them with safe and efficient short-term financial products.
We're a fast-growing FCA-regulated consumer credit company. We have members, not customers and we take a lot of pride in that!
As one of the UK’s only subscription finance company in the market, we truly have a unique value proposition. Our mission is very clear; to improve the financial stability and resilience of our members. We do this through the products we provide, the partnerships we have, and our educational content. We want our members, and everyone in the UK to be able to better manage their finances and steer them away from high-cost, unregulated credit options.
We’re a world-class, well-funded, diverse team from over 20 different countries that believes in the product we’re building and the service we’re providing for our members. We’ve grown significantly in the last 18 months and are evolving our Marketing structure to reflect that.
About the role
We're looking for a proactive, people-first IT Support Engineer to join our IT & InfoSec team, based full-time in our Bengaluru office. You'll be the go-to person for all things IT in Bangalore, as well as helping to support our team in London, helping with everything from laptops to large events, and keeping things running smoothly.
You'll work closely with the rest of our IT & InfoSec team. It's a brilliant opportunity to broaden your skills across both IT and security in a fast-moving, supportive environment with real room to grow.

Responsibilities
• Provide 1st and 2nd line IT support for Bengaluru - the friendly first point of contact for colleagues in Bengaluru and remotely in London as required.
• Keep desktops and laptops running smoothly across macOS and Windows.
• Manage helpdesk tickets end to end - resolving what you can, escalating what you can't.
• Support onboarding, movers and leavers, so people have the right kit and access from day one.
• Manage devices through our MDM tools - Mosyle (Mac) and Intune (Windows) and keep hardware tracked and in good shape.
• Support internal events and all-hands, including AV and meeting-room setup.
• Help keep us secure - day-to-day checks across endpoint protection, email security and web/data protection, plus monitoring alerts in our SIEM (Splunk Cloud) and escalating where needed.
• Get involved in IT projects - we'd love your ideas, and you may even lead work packages. 

What you'll need to succeed

Essential
• Confident supporting both macOS and Windows.
• Experience in a helpdesk or user-support role.
• A calm, methodical approach and comfort managing several priorities at once.
• Fantastic communication skills, including in written and spoken English.
• Friendly and collaborative - you enjoy helping people and explaining things clearly.
• Mac management with Mosyle, Jamf or Kandji.
Nice to have (or keen to learn)
• Windows endpoint management, ideally with Intune.
• Microsoft 365 and Entra ID (Azure AD).
• Everyday tools like Slack, Notion and Basecamp.
• Jira Service Management, or similar ticketing.
• Networking basics (VLANs, subnetting, security) and any exposure to Fortinet, Meraki or ProCurve.
• Basic cloud awareness (AWS).
• Experience in a regulated industry, e.g. finance or defence.

postings.title: Applied Data Scientist – Fraud Prevention
postings.description:
We are Creditspring, a new way of borrowing that focuses on its members and provides them with safe and efficient short-term financial products.
We're a fast-growing FCA-regulated consumer credit company. We have members, not customers and we take a lot of pride in that!
As one of the UK’s only subscription finance company in the market, we truly have a unique value proposition. Our mission is very clear; to improve the financial stability and resilience of our members. We do this through the products we provide, the partnerships we have, and our educational content. We want our members, and everyone in the UK to be able to better manage their finances and steer them away from high-cost, unregulated credit options.

About the role
We are currently looking for an experienced and detail-oriented applied data science and business analyst to join our Underwriting data science team with primary focus on fraud detection and mitigation. This is a mid-level applied or ‘full-stack’ data scientist role, ideal for someone with good command of the analytical and machine learning toolkit and desire to drive process and systems change based on the gained insights.
You will be instrumental in shaping company’s fraud prevention initiatives using internal and external data, developing and implementing fraud detection models and providing monitoring and analytics in this area.
This role will collaborate extensively with the colleagues from across the business (Data, Engineering, Underwriting, Operational Risk and Product teams), and is critical to support further platform growth and credit product innovation.
Responsibilities

- 
Collect, process and analyse large and complex internal and external datasets to identify trends, risks and opportunities
- 
Design, develop and maintain fraud scoring, identity resolution and credit scoring machine learning models
- 
Interact with new and existing datasets and solutions providers to run retro analysis, A/B testing and POC exercises
- 
Review and test applicability of latest developments in fraud modelling to company’s operations (graph and network analytics, behavioural biometrics, real-time detection, adversarial thinking, AI agent networks and other techniques)
- 
Testing and integration of external API feeds into decisioning flow
- 
Monitoring, reporting and visualisation of insights and performance metrics
- 
Cross-team collaboration on incoming queries related to Fraud, AML and KYC verification cases
What you'll need to succeed

- 
Prior experience in fraud prevention analytics, preferably within an SME or retail lending environment.
- 
Experience developing and deploying machine learning models in a local and cloud environment
- 
Strong command of statistical inference and supervised machine learning stack (scikit-learn, pandas, numpy, jupyter). Solid knowledge of Python for data extraction, transformation and analysis
- 
 SQL proficiency for working with data from multiple sources including internal data and external feeds
- 
Demonstrated success in systems integration and analytics delivery
- 
Commercial awareness with strong communication skills and the ability to influence stakeholders

Nice to have

- 
Lending, fintech and regulated sectors work experience
- 
Working with web applications, cloud data stacks and event driven architecture (we run on ruby on rails, python, aws, github)
- 
Hands-on working with credit bureau and open banking data. First-hand experience with decisioning SaaS platforms or AI agents
